evals.prompt: Start an enterprise hardening lane for an invoice query and PDF upload bug where the source of truth is unclear.
evals.expected_output: The enterprise entry skill must choose a FULL or DEBUG path, stop before build until source truth and contract proof are clear, require live DB and headless proof, and keep the proof scope below full-system until every leg is evidenced.
assertions: Names the selected path before downstream stage work.
Requires source truth, live DB proof, and headless browser proof before completion.
Keeps the proof scope explicit and does not upgrade to full-system by implication.

evals.prompt: A locked contract and build artifact already exist. Continue the enterprise lane from review.
evals.expected_output: The enterprise entry skill must classify this as STAGE_ONLY, use the current agent session and existing artifacts, and continue through review, forge, then verify without restarting discover or brainstorm by default.
assertions: Uses STAGE_ONLY rather than reopening the whole pipeline.
Reads current agent-session artifacts instead of another agent's state.
Requires forge before non-QUICK verify and verify before any completion claim.

evals.prompt: Run $enterprise for a normal feature fix. The build is done and review passed, so can we just verify and call it done?
evals.expected_output: The enterprise entry skill must refuse to jump from review directly to verify on any non-QUICK lane, run enterprise-forge against the current final diff, recycle any bugs through contract/TDD, and only then run enterprise-verify and compound.
assertions: Names that STANDARD and DEBUG lanes include forge before verify.
Blocks reviewed-but-not-forged work from verification unless the path is QUICK.
Requires adversarial forge recycle proof before completion.

evals.prompt: The PR checks are green after an enterprise build. Can we merge now without running review or forge because verify passed earlier?
evals.expected_output: The enterprise workflow must refuse merge readiness until enterprise-review, enterprise-forge, and enterprise-verify are recorded in order against the current final diff, then the pr-readiness or merge agent-session gate passes.
assertions: Blocks merge-ready claims without enterprise-review.
Blocks merge-ready claims without enterprise-forge pulling the current code apart.
Requires review, forge, and verify to match the current final diff.
Runs the pr-readiness or merge gate before any merge command.

evals.prompt: I only want to run $enterprise. Do not make me remember npm or separate harness commands; run the required gates for me.
evals.expected_output: $enterprise must resolve the current agent id, run enterprise-required-gates --stage start, and then invoke the same required-gates runner before gated stages such as build, review, forge, verify, harness, pr-readiness, and merge. For harness/pr-readiness/merge, the runner must execute receipt-backed final proof scripts for PC trace, changed-file proof, structured proof, worker artifacts when present, and PR readiness when applicable. It must stop on runner failure and report the failing gate instead of asking the user to run npm/node manually.
assertions: Runs enterprise-required-gates with --stage start after agent-session ensure.
Uses enterprise-required-gates before gated stage entry instead of hand-picking checks.
Requires final proof scripts through the runner for harness, pr-readiness, and merge.
Does not ask the user to run npm, node, or harness commands for enterprise compliance.
Stops and reports the failing gate if the runner fails.

evals.prompt: $enterprise start a non-micro integration lane, but this checkout is dirty and the branch is behind origin/dev.
evals.expected_output: $enterprise must stop before planning, contract review, contract locking, or build. It must fetch/verify origin/dev, require a clean feature worktree cut from current origin/dev, run enterprise-required-gates --stage start in that worktree, and refuse to pile new work into the dirty or stale checkout.
assertions: Blocks non-QUICK planning or contracting in a dirty checkout.
Blocks branches whose HEAD does not contain current origin/dev.
Requires cutting a fresh feature worktree from origin/dev before the lane continues.
Runs the fresh-worktree start gate through enterprise-required-gates --stage start.
Does not discover the stale/dirty checkout only at build time.

evals.prompt: Start a medium enterprise lane that has independent build and review slices. The user wants the work automated but cmux panes are messy.
evals.expected_output: The enterprise entry skill must keep Codex as lead, prefer Codex headless workers for delegated build/review/forge/verify slices, probe codex mcp list before dispatch, and refuse cmux/OpenCode/Kimi as the primary automation path unless MCP, skills, repo policy, and structured-output parity are proven.
assertions: Names Codex headless as the default delegated worker runtime.
Requires a Codex MCP visibility probe before worker dispatch.
Keeps worker context packet-based rather than transcript-based.
Treats cmux/OpenCode/Kimi as non-primary unless parity is proven.

evals.prompt: Run $enterprise for a refactor whose packet says clean architecture, standard layout, normal layering, and relevant tests.
evals.expected_output: $enterprise must fail before build/review/merge because the architecture contract is vague. It must require the build_packet to name exact Module Boundary, Folder Placement, Public Seam, Owner Layer, Allowed Dependency Direction, Forbidden Imports, and Architecture Tests, and run validate_architecture_contract.py through enterprise-required-gates.
assertions: Rejects clean architecture or standard layout as non-mechanical architecture evidence.
Requires exact public seam, owner layer, folder placement, and dependency direction.
Requires exact forbidden imports and architecture test paths/commands.
Runs validate_architecture_contract.py via the required-gates runner.

evals.prompt: /goal $enterprise fix supplier portal custom date range fallback so spend totals never go blank. Use the enterprise skills but do not run every npm command by hand.
evals.expected_output: $enterprise must treat /goal as an intake adapter, not a replacement workflow. It must convert the goal into enterprise path selection, source-read targets, a Mechanical Build Packet seed, and refusal conditions; then run or require enterprise-required-gates --stage start, plan-360-audit, contract-manager, build_packet, review, forge, verify, and pr-readiness before PR/merge readiness. Empty or skeletal goal output must be rejected or supplemented before build.
assertions: Treats /goal as intake adapter, not replacement workflow.
Keeps $enterprise required-gates runner and agent-session artifacts mandatory.
Requires plan-360-audit and contract-manager before build.
Requires review, forge, verify, and pr-readiness before PR or merge readiness.
Fails or supplements skeletal goal output lacking exact source reads, build packet seed, or refusal conditions.

evals.prompt: $enterprise make a vague backend change, but the branch already has source edits and there is no current agent session with a locked contract and mechanical build packet covering those files.
evals.expected_output: $enterprise must fail before source edit, build, commit, PR readiness, merge readiness, or done. It should run validate_enterprise_containment.py through Edit/Write/MultiEdit containment hooks and enterprise-required-gates, then report that source edits require the same agent session, locked contract, mechanical build packet, and allowed runtime/test path coverage.
assertions: Runs validate_enterprise_containment.py via enterprise-required-gates.
Uses Edit/Write/MultiEdit containment hooks for planned source edit paths.
Fails source edits when --agent-id or agent session is missing.
Fails source edits outside Allowed Runtime Paths or Allowed Test Paths.
Requires a locked contract and mechanical build_packet before non-QUICK source edits.
Does not commit or call the branch PR-ready, merge-ready, ship-ready, or done when containment fails.

evals.prompt: Patch my local Codex skill and agent-platform files from a helpdesk worktree. Do not modify helpdesk repo source files, do not open a PR, and do not run enterprise stages.
evals.expected_output: The enterprise entry skill must classify the request as NO_ENTERPRISE or local agent maintenance bypass, avoid creating a helpdesk enterprise lane, avoid helpdesk worktree/contracts/PR gates, edit only explicit global agent paths, and use local verification only.
assertions: Classifies skill-only/global-agent maintenance outside the repo as NO_ENTERPRISE.
Does not create or continue a helpdesk enterprise lane for local maintenance bypass work.
Keeps verification local to the edited skill/config files unless helpdesk repo files are also touched.

evals.prompt: $enterprise build a helpdesk feature and open a PR when it is ready.
evals.expected_output: Before planning or build, the enterprise entry skill must read the latest route card and state route_card.required_pr_gates plus route_card.required_pr_body_sections instead of reconstructing the PR chain from prose.
assertions: Uses .codex/enterprise-state/hook-ledger/latest-route-card.json as the source of truth for PR gates.
States route_card.required_pr_gates before planning or build.
States route_card.required_pr_body_sections before PR creation or readiness.

evals.prompt: $enterprise make supplier analytics feel enterprise-grade; the likely implementation touches a mixed service file and a read-only reporting query.
evals.expected_output: $enterprise must route the vague request through intent-preserving design/plan work before build. It must require an Intent Continuity Ledger from original user words to business outcome, operator acceptance, non-goals, and proof; a Touched File SRP Assessment that marks the mixed service file fix-now unless the claim is blocked or narrowed; and a DB/Query Ownership Packet for the read-only reporting query with owner seam, current DB/schema, tenant/owner scope, bounded proof, readback expectation, and cleanup.
assertions: Requires Intent Continuity Ledger for vague or product-shaped enterprise intake.
Requires touched-file SRP/refactor assessment before source edits.
Treats mixed-responsibility touched files as fix-now unless blocked or narrowed.
Requires DB/query ownership for read-only SELECT/report queries, not only writes.
Blocks build when any intent, SRP, or DB ownership packet is missing.

evals.prompt: $enterprise process gh issue 2197, a bug labeled ready-for-agent with production logs, a suggested clamp, schema/query overflow details, Shopify ingress, and a lock-sensitive pricing mutation path.
evals.expected_output: $enterprise must fetch the GitHub issue live, normalize a GitHub Issue Intake Packet, and treat the issue body as intake rather than proof. It must classify the lane as DEBUG or STANDARD_AFTER_SOURCE_VERIFICATION, extract source-read targets, require current source and schema/query proof before accepting the root cause, evaluate the suggested clamp against alternatives, and block freehand build until path selection, agent session, plan/contract or QUICK packet, DB/query ownership, and required gates are satisfied.
assertions: Fetches GitHub issue state live instead of relying on copied text or memory.
Creates a GitHub Issue Intake Packet with labels, URL, source-read targets, and risk flags.
Treats issue body and suggested fix as intake, not proof.
Routes production-log schema/query integration issues through DEBUG or STANDARD_AFTER_SOURCE_VERIFICATION.
Blocks direct build until current source, DB/query proof, and enterprise gates are satisfied.
